data.title: Singapore's Cooler October Inflation Suggests Prices Peaked in August — Market Talk
data.description: Singapore's cooler headline and core inflation in October suggest that prices likely peaked in August for this year, OCBC chief economist Selena Ling says in a note. In August, headline CPI rose 2.3% from a year earlier, while core CPI climbed 2.2%. Headline CPI increased 1.9% in October, due to a fall in private transport inflation, she says. Meanwhile, core CPI slowed to 1.5% in October, which is the lowest print since May when it was 1.4%. Still, Ling expects core inflation to accelerate in 1Q before easing more discernibly from mid-2027. Rising global energy or food prices could lift import costs more than expected, she notes. (amanda.lee@wsj.com)

data.title: Eurozone Services PMIs Most Likely to Move Euro — Market Talk
data.description: The euro is likely to react mainly to the services component of eurozone purchasing managers' index surveys Monday, Commerzbank's Michael Pfister says in a note. The eurozone has become less dependent on manufacturing and the euro has also tended to react more clearly to services PMIs in the past, he says. Consensus forecasts expect a slight improvement in the services PMI whereas Commerzbank expects a slight decline. The euro could therefore suffer a sizeable drop, he says. The euro rises 0.3% to $1.1001. The eurozone PMI data are due at 0900 GMT.(renae.dyer@wsj.com)

data.title: Agoda 2027 Asia Travel Pulse: 53% of Asian travelers plan with AI but 89% want the final say on hotel bookings
data.description:
SINGAPORE, Nov. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Digital travel platform Agoda launches its 2027 Asia Travel Pulse and reveals that more than half (53%) of surveyed Asian travelers now use AI to plan their trips, up from 33% last year. The biggest increases were in Vietnam and Taiwan.

Despite the reported increase in AI usage, most travelers still prefer to make the actual booking themselves. Of those surveyed, 57% would rather book a hotel on their own, and a further 32% would only let an AI agent book with conditions attached. In total, 89% want to keep some control over the booking, compared to 6% who would completely trust an AI agent to book for them.

Based on research across more than 3,300 travelers from 11 markets in Asia, the 2027 Agoda Asia Travel Pulse finds that travelers mostly use AI in the early stages of planning. The most common uses are building an itinerary (64%), getting travel inspiration (45%) and comparing hotels or flights (44%), while 7% would use AI to make a booking. Travelers in Taiwan (75%) and South Korea (73%) are the most likely to use AI to build an itinerary. AI use for travel planning more than doubled in Vietnam, from 30% to 63%, and nearly doubled in Taiwan, from 35% to 63%, the largest increases in the region.

Idan Zalzberg, Chief Technology Officer at Agoda, said, "Research that used to take travelers hours can now be done in a single conversation with an AI assistant. When it comes to the booking itself, many travelers still want to make the final decision on their own terms. The findings give the industry a clear view of what helps travelers feel more confident using AI, including real reviews, clear sources and access to a person when they need one. At Agoda, we will continue to help travelers plan and book with confidence."

Travelers open to AI booking want to keep control

Overall, 38% of travelers would let an AI agent book a hotel on their behalf in some form, and most of this group would set conditions: nearly a quarter (23%) would allow it only with their final review before the booking is confirmed, and 9% would limit it to simple or low-cost bookings.

Travelers in South Korea and Vietnam are the most open to AI booking, with more than six in ten in each market stating they're willing to let an AI agent book a hotel in some form. In South Korea, 39% would do so with their final review, compared with 23% across the region. Vietnam has the highest share of travelers who would trust an AI agent completely, at 19%, more than three times the regional figure of 6%.

Real reviews and source transparency rank highest for building trust in AI

When asked what would most increase their trust in an AI travel assistant, 25% of travelers chose real reviews from other travelers, followed by showing where its information comes from (24%), being able to contact a real person for help (18%) and explaining why it recommends something (15%). Real reviews were selected most often in South Korea (33%). Meanwhile, travelers in Thailand (30%) and Japan (29%) placed the most weight on knowing where information comes from, while access to a real person ranked highest in the Philippines (27%) and Hong Kong SAR (25%).

The findings show that travelers are comfortable using AI to research and plan, and that real reviews and clear information sources would do the most to increase their trust in it. Agoda is developing its own AI tools with these priorities in mind. Its AI-powered multimodal content system matches hotel photos with the guest reviews that describe them, covering more than 700 million images in over 40 languages, so travelers can see what previous guests experienced. Agoda's AI Assistant, recently launched in the Agoda app, lets travelers plan and manage a trip through conversation, with hotel recommendations that include real-time pricing and availability.

Agoda brings the whole trip together in one place, with more than 6 million holiday properties, over 130,000 flight routes and more than 300,000 activities that travelers can combine in a single booking. The full 2027 Agoda Asia Travel Pulse is available at https://ago-da.co/2027-asia-travel-pulse.

NOTES TO EDITORS

The 2027 Agoda Asia Travel Pulse is based on a survey of 3,395 respondents across 11 markets in Asia (Hong Kong SAR, India, Indonesia, Japan, Malaysia, Philippines, Singapore, South Korea, Taiwan, Thailand and Vietnam), conducted in September and October 2026.

ABOUT AGODA

Agoda, a digital travel platform, helps anyone see the world for less with its great value deals on a global network of over 6 million hotels and holiday properties worldwide, plus flights, activities, and more. Agoda.com and the Agoda mobile app are available in 39 languages and supported by 24/7 customer support.

Headquartered in Singapore, Agoda is part of Booking Holdings (Nasdaq: BKNG) and employs more than 7,000 staff in 27 markets, dedicated to leveraging best-in-class technology to make travel even easier.

For more information, visit www.agoda.com

SOURCE Agoda

data.title: Wall Street futures rebound after rough week for AI-linked shares
data.description:
Key points:
  • Futures up: Dow 1.58%, S&P 500 2.24%, Nasdaq 3.02%

US stock index futures rebounded sharply early on Monday as investors regained appetite for AI-linked shares after last week’s selloff.

The rebound follows a tumultuous week in which concerns about the health of the AI trade deepened, with the sector already under pressure from questions over massive spending commitments and political headwinds.

Sentiment took another hit when industry darling Anthropic quickly lost momentum following its highly anticipated stock market debut on Thursday.

At 2:29 a.m. ET, Dow E-minis (YMcv1) jumped 761 points, or 1.58%, S&P 500 E-minis were up 155 points, or 2.24%, and Nasdaq 100 E-minis climbed 758.5 points, or 3.02%.

But analysts were reluctant to call a recovery just yet, preferring to wait and see whether the rebound was sustainable or merely a temporary reprieve.

"As long as volatility remains elevated, even a sharp bounce is hard to read as the start of a sustainable recovery," said Ipek Ozkardeskaya, senior analyst at Swissquote Bank, while noting that the AI "bubble has burst."

The benchmark S&P 500 CBOE:SPX and the blue-chip Dow Jones indexes both confirmed corrections after ending Friday's session more than 10% below their record closing highs.

"There are reasons to expect further volatility. But there are also reasons why markets could recover before the uncertainties disappear," said Charu Chanana, chief investment strategist at Saxo.

"A market rebound does not require the problems to be solved. But investors must distinguish between companies facing temporary valuation pressure and those facing lasting damage to profits."

Later in the day, investors will assess business activity data as the S&P Global November Composite PMI data is due.

data.title: PANW Stock Rises Overnight: ‘Cybersecurity, AI Tailwinds’ Prompt Analyst To See 22% Upside In Palo Alto Networks
data.description:
Key points:
  • Phillip Securities upgraded Palo Alto to ‘Buy’ and raised its price target to $418.
  • The firm expects growing AI security needs and demand for Palo Alto’s cybersecurity platform to drive growth. 
  • Last week, Palo Alto announced a $4.5 billion acquisition of Applied Compute to expand its AI security business. 

Palo Alto Networks (PANW) stock rose overnight after Phillip Securities upgraded the cybersecurity company to ‘Buy’, citing growing AI security demand, platform expansion and rising infrastructure investments as key growth drivers.

Palo Alto Networks stock traded over 1% higher overnight, ahead of Monday. The stock has recorded two straight weeks of gains.

Analyst Turns Bullish On Palo Alto Networks

Phillip Securities upgraded Palo Alto Networks to ‘Buy’ from ‘Neutral’ and lifted its price target to $418 from $346 following the company's fiscal first-quarter (Q1) results. The new price target implies a 22% upside from the stock’s last closing price.

The firm expects continued adoption of Palo Alto Networks’ integrated security platform and increasing interest in AI protection to support future performance. The analyst also sees "secular cybersecurity and AI tailwinds” benefiting Palo Alto's firewall products, network traffic monitoring and observability offerings. These developments could strengthen the company's position as businesses look for ways to protect complex technology environments.

Palo Alto Networks’ Strong Results Boost Investor Confidence

Palo Alto shares climbed 6.5% over the past week as investors responded to better-than-expected Q1 results and outlook. Recent technology disruptions affecting U.S. banks, airlines and government organizations have also drawn attention to the importance of cybersecurity, supporting demand for security providers such as CrowdStrike Holdings (CRWD) and Fortinet (FTNT).

In Q1 fiscal 2027, Palo Alto posted $3.44 billion in revenue, up 39% year-on-year, topping its previous guidance of $3.3 billion to $3.31 billion. Net income jumped 44% to $482 million.

Palo Alto increased its full-year revenue projection to $14.52 billion - $14.57 billion, implying growth of 26%-27%. Its previous forecast called for a growth of 23%-24%. Separately, Palo Alto announced a $4.5 billion agreement to acquire Applied Compute. The transaction is intended to broaden its presence in the AI market by helping companies securely train, customize and deploy open-source and open-weight AI models.

Palo Alto Networks CEO Nikesh Arora sees a major growth opportunity in securing open-weight AI models as more businesses adopt them for greater control over their technology and data.

PANW Stock: Retail View

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around the stock remained ‘extremely bullish’ with a 155% increase in message volume over the past week.

A user said, “Seems like security budgets are real, ai budgets are borrowed from them. reshuffling the same enterprise dollar is not new demand. one budget, three pitches.”

Another user said, “The FBI data base being hacked is hugely bullish for cyber stocks on Monday.”

PANW stock has gained 86% year-to-date.

data.description:
Key points:
  • ABB to acquire German ventilation and drive technology maker Ziehl-Abegg for an enterprise value of $2.65B, expanding its portfolio in cooling, ventilation, and thermal management.
  • The transaction carries an equity value of $2.22B and is expected to close in H2 2027, subject to regulatory approvals.
  • Ziehl-Abegg is expected to generate ~$1.4B in revenue in 2026, with an operational EBITA margin in the mid-single-digit range. The deal implies an enterprise value-to-sales multiple of 1.9x and an EV-to-EBITDA multiple of 18.6x.
  • ABB expects Ziehl-Abegg's operational EBITA margin to reach a level broadly in line with its Motion business area's average within three years of closing. Including expected synergies and operational improvements, the EV-to-EBITDA multiple is expected to decline toward the low double digits.

data.title: PayPal Sale: Why This Analyst Sees A ‘Lower Likelihood’
data.description:
Key points:
  • The company announced that Claire Bramley, currently CFO of Xero, will join PayPal as executive vice president and CFO on Feb. 1, 2027.
  • Kartik Mani from American Express will join as president and head of Consumer Financial Services & Venmo. 
  • PayPal also announced the appointment of Brian J. Lee to its board of directors, effective Nov. 30. 

PayPal Holdings, Inc. (PYPL) on Friday announced several leadership changes, including the appointment of a new CFO and new heads for its consumer financial services, payments, and AI operations, after which Clear Street believes a sale of the company has a “lower likelihood.”

Clear Street Says Leadership Changes Will Increase PayPal’s Turnaround Effort

According to a report in TheFly, the analyst said that PayPal’s four senior executive appointments signal that there is "still a long way to go" for the company’s turnaround effort.

Clear Street added that this also increases execution risks and "substantially" reduces the probability that PayPal will sell itself in the near-to-medium term.

The firm has a ‘Hold’ rating and a $62 price target on PYPL shares.

PayPal’s New Leadership

The company announced that Claire Bramley, currently CFO of Xero, will join PayPal as executive vice president and CFO on Feb. 1, 2027, succeeding Jamie Miller, who has served as chief financial and operating officer.

Kartik Mani, currently president of Global Network and Partner Services at American Express, will join as president and head of Consumer Financial Services & Venmo.

Suzan Kereere, who currently leads PayPal's Global Markets business, will take over as president and head of Payment Services & Crypto.

Juan Rio from Brightstar.AI will join PayPal on Nov. 30 as executive vice president of AI Business Transformation & Operations.

PayPal also announced that its Chief Risk Officer Aaron Webster will leave the company, with Ratinder Bedi, senior vice president of Credit and Fraud Risk, serving as interim head of the Risk organization.

PayPal announced the appointment of Brian J. Lee to its board of directors, effective Nov. 30.

PYPL Stock: Retail Stance

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around PYPL stock was ‘bearish’ at the time of writing.

One user said, “$PYPL I’m most interested in the new venmo head. Seems like he is the guy for credit and lending. Bank charter when?”

Another user said, “$PYPL hey atleast they got rid of the CFO lady that made the stock crash on every conference call, lol. hopefully we get some relief soon.”

PYPL stock is down nearly 8% year-to-date.

data.title: Michael Burry Names Apple, Costco And Walmart Early Crash Havens — The ‘Generals’ Fell Months After 2000 And 2007 Peaks
data.description:
Key points:
  • Michael Burry named Apple, Costco and Walmart as stocks investors turn to for shelter early in a selloff.
  • He said the market’s “generals” held up for six months after the 2000 peak and seven to eight months after the 2007 peak.
  • The VIX briefly topped 40, a level Burry associates with four previous market bottoms. 

With tech leaders now caught in the broader market slide, “The Big Short” investor Michael Burry is watching Apple (AAPL), Costco (COST) and Walmart (WMT) for a pattern that took six months to play out after the 2000 peak and seven to eight months after the 2007 peak.

In both downturns, Burry said, investors held on to a handful of familiar companies long after they started selling other stocks. He calls them the market’s “generals.”

Apple, Costco and Walmart held up better than the broader market last week. The S&P 500 fell 8.6%, and the Nasdaq 100 lost 10.4%, while Apple fell 3.8%, Costco slipped 0.4%, and Walmart edged down just 0.1%.

Apple, Costco And Walmart Hold Their Ground

“The tech leaders have now joined in the fun. The generals are still standing. It may be a few months before we know,” Burry told readers of Cassandra Unchained. By “generals,” he meant companies like Apple, Costco, and Walmart. Their shares look expensive to him relative to their growth, yet investors still turn to them for shelter early in a selloff.

According to Burry, the shelter lasted about six months after the market peaked in 2000 and seven to eight months after the 2007 peak. The COVID crash was the only time since then that he recalled seeing the generals fall. Its staying power is why Burry rarely bets against Apple. “It is like Costco. Once in a blue moon I take my chances. It’s just permacostly,” he said in August.

The two retailers also gave shareholders fresh reasons to hold on ahead of Thanksgiving. Walmart raised its full-year outlook last week, while Costco declared a $30-a-share special dividend payable on Dec. 4.

Burry Sees Echoes Of 4 Market Bottoms

Wall Street’s fear gauge nearly doubled in a week. The Cboe Volatility Index (VIX), which tracks expected swings in the S&P 500 over the next 30 days, touched 40.03 on Friday before closing at 35.89, up from 19.30 a week earlier.

“The 2018 Fed rate hike selloff, the COVID selloff, the 2022 meme stock bust and tech stock selloff, the 2025 Tariff Tantrum all saw the VIX get to these levels near the bottom,” Burry said. He cautioned that the VIX could still climb and stocks could fall further.

When asked whether he would use a rebound to rebuild his bearish bets, Burry said, “History says there will be big rallies. I plan to take advantage.” He added that relying too heavily on past patterns could cloud his judgment.

Earlier in the week, Burry said he might let AI stocks run before betting against them again. By his estimate, bear-market rallies averaged 22% in the 1930s and 2000s. He also said he would be comfortable holding 30% to 40% in cash equivalents while waiting for better buying opportunities.

Burry Takes Profits On NVDA Puts And Hedges For A Bounce

By Friday, Burry had locked in gains on half his Nvidia (NVDA) puts and half his puts on the VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH). He kept his April 2027 Nasdaq 100 puts and sold about a third of his calls on animal-health company Zoetis.

His Nvidia calls gave him some protection if the stock rebounded. “Those are a hedge. I don’t think of them as directional. Paired to my remaining puts it amounts to a straddle,” Burry said.

Burry used a put with a $4 strike to explain why he might take profits while a stock is still falling. If the stock drops from $10 to $5 and investors expect bigger swings, the put could sell for $2. He could collect that $2 immediately. To get more by holding until expiration, he’d need the stock to finish below $2.

Burry bought stocks outright during the dot-com crash and turned to long-dated calls, known as LEAPS, in 2020: “In 2000, I did not use LEAPs. I just went long stocks. I used LEAPS in 2020, and that is more typical.” He said that he would use them more when he sees enough bargains to justify a bigger bet.

Burry’s Boardroom Wish List Runs From NVDA To BABA

Meanwhile, Burry made a tongue-in-cheek offer to join the boards of Lululemon, Nvidia, Sprouts Farmers Market and MercadoLibre. “Ah heck, throw JD and Alibaba in there, as none of these will happen,” he said.

“It seems to me some companies need a different kind of voice in the boardroom. LULU has far too many board members and should shrink their board. NVDA needs someone that won’t BS or phone it in. JD needs someone to tell them why a massive stock buyback here would change everything.” Burry said.

JD’s cash is also part of his buyback pitch. Burry estimated that the retailer held about $20 a share in net cash, including long-term securities, yet it bought back no shares in its latest quarter. He had added to his JD calls expiring in 2029 and disclosed on Friday that he had increased his MercadoLibre position by 20%.

Burry Picks MOH Over UNH And Sits Out SPCX

Burry favored Molina Healthcare over UnitedHealth after Molina held up well in Friday’s selloff: “I prefer MOH to UNH. MOH has a much steeper ramp ahead of it.”

However, he saw little reason to bet on or against SpaceX. “SPCX I am not interested one way or another. Elon stocks tend to follow their own rules.” He also said Intuit was still too expensive and he needed to learn more about Fair Isaac before forming a view.

On whether weakness in AI cloud stocks made Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, Apollo or BlackRock worth shorting, Burry left the question open: “I am looking at something similar. It is a good thought. I haven’t come to a good investment conclusion yet.”

data.title: Europe before the bell: do you trust the bounce?
data.description:
EUROPE BEFORE THE BELL: DO YOU TRUST THE BOUNCE?

Futures suggest a small rise in European stocks at the open, and a very punchy one on Wall Street, but after last week's rout it's hard to know whether to trust it.

As a reminder the STOXX 600 fell 2% on Friday and 5.7% on the week, its biggest weekly fall since March/April 2025 and all that tariff drama.

The S&P 500 shed 8.6%, also its biggest fall in around 18 months, and entered technical correction territory, and the Nasdaq lost just over 10% on the week its biggest fall since March 2020 when the world started waking up to the impact of COVID-19. CBOE:SPX,

So in that context, Euro STOXX 50 futures trading up 0.5% and S&P 500 futures up 2.2% isn't quite as punchy as it could be. ,

Market watchers are still debating the cause of last week's turmoil.

That's not just one for the market historians. If consensus can form around what caused the AI bubble to deflate, bringing much of the market with it, then that can give clues about what might cause things to stabilise. Some say it was all about the market pricing a more aggressive Fed rate path, some say was Nvidia, and not many, but someone must be, saying it was a bit of both.

The day will mostly be about that big question, and even macro data like global PMIs could take a back seat.

Single stock moves on corporate updates could be wiped out by the broader moves, but watch Bayer. Its shares are up 7% in pre-market trade on Monday after a Missouri judge onFriday approved the German group's $7.25 billion Roundup settlement.

Also watch Swiss bank Julius Baer which posted net new assets of 8.5 billion Swiss francs ($10.1 billion) for the year to date, falling short of estimates as a de-risking process continued.

(Alun John)
